newsitem.title: USA: Panetta says no decision on running for governor.
newsitem.headline: Panetta says no decision on running for governor.

text.p: President Clinton's retiring chief of staff Leon Panetta said Friday he will make no decision on whether to run for governor of California until after he actually leaves the White House job in January.
"I have not made a decision nor will I make a decision on this issue as long as I am chief of staff to the president of the United States," Panetta said at the National Press Club.
"When I get back to California, obviously that will be the time when I'll think about whether or not to do that."
The San Francisco Chronicle quoted Panetta, 58, earlier this week as saying he will explore whether to seek the Democratic nomination to challenge California Republican Gov. Pete Wilson in 1998.

Panetta said in a press club speech that there was no way to foresee whether the newly re-elected Republican Congress and Democratic President Clinton will spend the next four years in crippling confrontation or some degree of cooperation -- but he indicated scepticism.

He told reporters after the speech, as he has said before, that Clinton and Republicans could complete negotiations on balancing the budget in a month but Republicans are asking Clinton for a whole new budget balancing plan. He said that would push off agreement for at least six or seven months.

Panetta also said it was questionable whether Congress would break a cycle of inaction on campaign finance reform despite allegations of scandal and loopholes that poured millions of dollars to support presidential and congressional candidates above federal campaign spending limits this year.
But Panetta said, "I think in the end what will happen here is that the American people will not tolerate the continuation of the existing system.
"How soon that message gets across and how soon they are willing to get it done, I think, is going to depend on the leadership, both the president and the Congress, in pushing it forward," he said.
